script.spoken: Why one loose wire killed 35 people. In 1988, a signal near Clapham Junction showed the wrong aspect. Old wiring had been left in place and not secured. A crowded train ran into another; 484 people were injured. The technician was in his 13th straight seven-day week. His work had never been independently checked. That's why rail safety depends on a second pair of eyes.
